date_note: The NZ Herald article is dated 24 November and says chief executive Grant McKenzie confirmed the attack early Tuesday; it gives no earlier day.
exec: A New Zealand publisher says a cyber-attack disrupted its production systems, and the NZ Herald reports that at least two newspaper editions will not be published.
geo_basis: headquarters city of Allied Press (Dunedin); the Herald piece describes a South Island-wide impact
plain: A cyber-attack disrupted production at New Zealand publisher Allied Press. The NZ Herald reports the Greymouth Star and Hokitika Guardian editions would not be published, and other papers would be late.

sources.name: Otago Daily Times (Allied Media statement, Paul McIntyre), 24 Nov 2026

summary: Allied Media (Allied Press) said in its own statement that it was the target of a cyber attack that disrupted several production systems, delaying delivery of community papers by a day, and that it has no evidence customer information has been accessed. The NZ Herald reports the Greymouth Star and Hokitika Guardian editions would not be published.
title: Cyber-attack disrupts Allied Press production; Greymouth Star and Hokitika Guardian editions not published, NZ Herald reports

validation.note: Corroborated by two publishers: the Otago Daily Times (carrying the primary Allied Media statement) and the NZ Herald, which each state the attack and the disruption.
